visible_bad_hover: public colour-key legend rendered a white panel with near-white label text in dark mode (measured WCAG contrast 1.22:1; AA needs >=4.5:1); colour swatches rendered transparent
corrected_hover_or_pending_reason: panel/toggle use the real theme tokens (surface/text/border/shadow); labels use theme text (not pale role colour); swatches inherit the mode-scoped grammar palette so chips match running text; contrast 12.63:1 dark / 14.75:1 light
what_failed: legend styled with token names that do not exist in the theme engine, so it fell back to hardcoded white in BOTH modes while the text token was theme-aware and went near-white in dark; separately the grammar-colour vars were out of scope for the legend subtree so chips were transparent
learner_explanation: a grammar colour cue that is invisible in your theme teaches nothing; a colour key must be readable in light and dark, and each swatch must show the same colour the word is painted in the running text
drill_prompt: Given a learner-facing colour legend, verify: (1) panel background differs from page background in both themes (proves theme-aware, not hardcoded); (2) title + every label >= 4.5:1 contrast vs panel; (3) each swatch is distinguishable by fill, border, or a neutral ring. Which check catches a white-panel-in-dark-mode regression?

visible_bad_hover: styled a teaching surface with a remembered generic-kit token name (--du-surface) that is not defined in the live token file (real name: --du-panel)
corrected_hover_or_pending_reason: grep the live token file for the exact token names before authoring; a non-existent CSS var silently falls back and desyncs from the theme
what_failed: authored from memory of a generic glass kit instead of the project token file
learner_explanation: the same discipline as never authoring a gloss from a remembered root: verify against the source of truth (token file / Qamus entry), never memory
drill_prompt: A panel uses background:var(--du-surface,#fff). The token file defines --du-panel, not --du-surface. What renders in dark mode, and why?
